title: INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED in mse_loss when mixing CPU and CUDA tensors

labels.name: module: error checking
labels.description: Bugs related to incorrect/lacking error checking

labels.name: triaged
labels.description: This issue has been looked at a team member, and triaged and prioritized into an appropriate module

body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Calling nn.MSELoss() with a mix of CUDA and CPU tensors leads to an internal assert failure inside PyTorch's CUDA backend instead of a standard Python RuntimeError.

## Program

```python
import torch
import numpy as np
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.distributions.normal as norm
device = torch.device(('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu'))
print('Using {}'.format(device))
m = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(1, 128).cuda(), nn.Tanh(), nn.Linear(128, 128).cuda(), nn.Tanh(), nn.Linear(128, 128).cuda(), nn.Tanh())
m.to(device, dtype=None, non_blocking=False)
opt = torch.optim.Adam(m.parameters(), lr=0.001)
print('Number of trainable parameters: ', sum((p.numel() for p in m.parameters() if p.requires_grad)))
input_tensor = torch.tensor(77.0, device=device)
target = torch.tensor(66.0)
loss_function = nn.MSELoss()
print('Loss Function: ', loss_function)
loss = loss_function(input_tensor, target)
print('Initial loss: ', loss)
for epoch in range(20):
    yhat = m(input_tensor)
    loss = loss_function(yhat, target)
    print('epoch {}, loss {}'.format(epoch, loss))
    loss.backward()
    opt.step()
    opt.zero_grad()
```
